text: The Tyrell House at 64 King Street, York, was built in 1859 and was the home of William Tyrell, the first reeve of Weston. It was also the birthplace of Joseph and William Tyrrell, who both became explorers, leading expeditions to survey areas of northern and western Canada. The Weston community values the heritage of this property very highly and they are interested in ensuring that it remains a historical touchstone. The designation By-law 2970-78 for this property was passed by Council in 1978. By-law 2970-78 complied with the provisions of the Ontario Heritage Act at that time. The Ontario Heritage Act has been amended since 1978, and it now requires that designation By-laws include a statement explaining the cultural heritage value or interest of the property and a description of the property's heritage attributes.
